calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
calls.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill is around the middle of the league, and the Panthers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight. The Sharks take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.beyond: Florida is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 238 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 142 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: San Jose couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose usually gets better looks than most teams. Not tonight: a 3.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.7% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Cagnoni ends it in overtime
paras: Ivar Stenberg played his first NHL game. Mason Marchment made his Sharks debut, after playing for the Blue Jackets. Brady Tkachuk and Jacob Trouba fought midway through the first, and Marchment opened the scoring for the Sharks late in the period. Will Smith scored early in the second and again less than five minutes later to stretch the lead to 3-0. Collin Graf and Uvis Balinskis dropped the gloves midway through the period, and Eetu Luostarinen got the Panthers on the board on the power play late in the period. Luostarinen and Matthew Tkachuk scored just 17 seconds apart early in the third to tie it 3-3. Luca Cagnoni, in his tenth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Smith, in overtime to win it. There were two three-point nights: Macklin Celebrini with three assists, and Smith with two goals and an assist.

The Sharks outshot the Panthers 32-26, but the Panthers’ chances were the better ones. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Panthers win about six in ten. Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves for the Sharks, and Akira Schmid stopped 28 of 32.
The Panthers hit two posts and still lost. The Sharks improved to 1-0-0, and the Cats dropped to 1-0-1.

items.text: The Sharks opened their season with a win at home.
Brady Tkachuk’s five-game point streak against San Jose ended.
All three of the preview’s calls held.
